title: The Wonderful City of Oz, part 10
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: The Lion was angry at this speech, but could say nothing in reply, and while he stood silently gazing at the Ball of Fire it became so furiously hot that he turned tail and rushed from the room. He was glad to find his friends waiting for him, and told them of his terrible interview with the Wizard.
“What shall we do now?” asked Dorothy sadly.
“There is only one thing we can do,” returned the Lion, “and that is to go to the land of the Winkies, seek out the Wicked Witch, and destroy her.”
“But suppose we cannot?” said the girl.
“Then I shall never have courage,” declared the Lion.
“And I shall never have brains,” added the Scarecrow.
“And I shall never have a heart,” spoke the Tin Woodman.
“And I shall never see Aunt Em and Uncle Henry,” said Dorothy, beginning to cry.
“Be careful!” cried the green girl. “The tears will fall on your green silk gown and spot it.”
So Dorothy dried her eyes and said, “I suppose we must try it; but I am sure I do not want to kill anybody, even to see Aunt Em again.”
“I will go with you; but I’m too much of a coward to kill the Witch,” said the Lion.
“I will go too,” declared the Scarecrow; “but I shall not be of much help to you, I am such a fool.”
“I haven’t the heart to harm even a Witch,” remarked the Tin Woodman; “but if you go I certainly shall go with you.”

Therefore it was decided to start upon their journey the next morning, and the Woodman sharpened his axe on a green grindstone and had all his joints properly oiled. The Scarecrow stuffed himself with fresh straw and Dorothy put new paint on his eyes that he might see better. The green girl, who was very kind to them, filled Dorothy’s basket with good things to eat, and fastened a little bell around Toto’s neck with a green ribbon.

They went to bed quite early and slept soundly until daylight, when they were awakened by the crowing of a green cock that lived in the back yard of the Palace, and the cackling of a hen that had laid a green egg.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Lion leave the Throne Room?
options: He turned tail and rushed out
He walked out slowly, roaring
He was carried out by the soldier
He stayed until the fire went out

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what does the Lion say is the only thing they can do?
options: Go to the land of the Winkies and destroy the Witch
Leave the Emerald City and go home
Ask the Wizard once more for mercy
Send word to the Good Witch of the North

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the green girl call out to Dorothy?
options: Her tears would spot the green silk gown
The Wizard was calling for her
The Lion had come back from the Wizard
It was time to leave the palace

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Woodman do to prepare?
options: Sharpened his axe and had his joints oiled
Built a new truck for the journey
Filled his oil-can from the palace stores
Made a raft to cross the river again

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy do for the Scarecrow?
options: Put new paint on his eyes
Stuffed him with fresh straw
Mended the tear in his coat
Made him a new pointed hat

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how do the three companions offer their help?
options: Each admits he will be of little use, but goes anyway
Each promises to kill the Witch single-handed
Each asks Dorothy to release him from the journey
Each insists the others should go instead

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Dorothy say about the killing?
options: That she does not want to kill anybody, even to see Aunt Em
That she will do it gladly if it takes her home
That she will leave it to the Lion to manage
That she no longer believes the Witch exists

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what would each of them lose if they fail?
options: Courage, brains, a heart, and a way home
Only Dorothy's chance of reaching Kansas
The gifts the Wizard has already given them
Their rooms and welcome in the palace

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the green girl was very kind to them?
options: She did thoughtful things to help them on their way
She spoke to them gently but did nothing
She agreed to travel with them to the West
She asked the Wizard to spare them the task

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: Four who each doubt themselves agree to go anyway, and prepare
Four travellers decide the task is impossible and stay
The Wizard relents and offers to help them himself
The green girl persuades them not to leave the city

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the green girl put round Toto's neck?
options: A little bell on a green ribbon
A collar of woven emeralds
A green silk apron
Nothing; she filled the basket instead

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the green girl fill Dorothy's basket with?
options: Good things to eat
Green spectacles
Paint for the Scarecrow
Oil for the Woodman

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Scarecrow say about his own usefulness?
options: That he would not be much help, being such a fool
That he would lead the party to the West
That he alone could outwit the Wicked Witch
That he would rather stay in the city

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why could the Lion say nothing in reply to Oz?
options: He was angry, but the fire grew too hot to bear
He had promised Dorothy that he would not argue
The Wizard had already vanished from the throne
He had lost his voice from roaring in the forest

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Tin Woodman say about harming a Witch?
options: That he has not the heart for it, but will go with them
That he will strike the first blow himself
That a witch cannot be harmed by an axe
That he would rather stay behind

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does grindstone refer to?
options: A stone used for sharpening the axe
A stone set into the palace floor
A green gem from the Throne Room
A weight for holding the raft down

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A reluctant decision, and careful preparation for a hard journey
A refusal to go, and a decision to stay in the palace
A quarrel in which the party breaks apart
A promise from the Wizard to travel with them
